library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Centanni_2024_vincristine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Centanni_2024_vincristine"))$description`
* Simulation variant: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Centanni_2024_vincristine_mipd"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-023-01336-1> (open access)

Centanni et al. re-analysed the vincristine concentrations of the randomized
bolus-versus-infusion trial of van de Velde et al. 2020 (see
`vandeVelde_2020_vincristine`) and linked them to the CTCAE grades of
vincristine-induced peripheral neuropathy (VIPN) recorded after every dose.
The paper contributes two model files:

* `Centanni_2024_vincristine` -- the final estimated models: the PK model of
  Table 2 and the VIPN model of Table 3. Each dosing occasion was a separate
  individual when the PK model was fitted, so the 76.6% IIV on CL also
  carries the occasion-to-occasion variability.
* `Centanni_2024_vincristine_mipd` -- the same model with the CL terms of the
  paper's second-stage estimation, which split the per-occasion CL estimates
  into IIV (32.3%) and inter-occasion variability (36.3%) and fitted a
  two-group CYP3A5 mixture (42.3 L/h/70 kg in 90% of patients, 1.87-fold
  higher in 10%). The paper used it to generate the true exposures of its
  precision-dosing simulations (Table 4, Figures 3-5).

The PK model is two-compartmental with allometric weight scaling. The
infusion arm has a lag time from bag to bloodstream and an infusion that
lasts 1.30 times the documented duration (flushing), and its samples carry a
larger residual error with IIV. The VIPN model is a proportional-odds model
with a Markov element, applied to each of four CTCAE subscores (peripheral
sensory neuropathy, peripheral motor neuropathy, constipation, neuralgia) on
three levels (grade 0, 1, >= 2):

* `logit P(grade >= 1) = B1 + Emax x AUC / (AUC50 + AUC) + B>0 x [previous grade > 0]`
* `logit P(grade >= 2) = logit P(grade >= 1) + B2`
* `B1` is `B1|0` on the first dosing occasion and `B1|0, if OCC > 1` from the
  second; `B2` is shared by neuralgia and motor neuropathy and by
  constipation and sensory neuropathy (Table 3).
* `AUC = dose / CL` of the current occasion, in ng\*h/mL.

The model outputs `p_vipn_ge1` (all subscores), `p_vipn_ge2_nm` (neuralgia
and motor) and `p_vipn_ge2_cs` (constipation and sensory). The Markov state
enters through the `PREV_AE_SCORE` covariate, the occasion through `CYCLE`.
A later analysis by the same group (Centanni et al. 2026, CPT
Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol, doi:10.1002/psp4.70303) re-estimated a
related model and printed its NONMEM code; that code builds the logits the
same way (grade >= 2 logit = grade >= 1 logit + increment, previous-grade
term inside the grade >= 1 logit, constipation and sensory sharing one
increment), which supports the reading above.

# Population

Table 1 describes 35 children (median age 9 years, range 2-17; median weight
34 kg, range 12-95; median BSA 1.2 m^2, range 0.5-2.2; 16 male). 64% were
treated for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Twenty were randomized to an IV
bolus and fifteen to an infusion (standard 60 min of which 38 min of drug and
22 min of flushing; 96 min in four and 15 min in two patients). Doses were
1.5 or 2 mg/m^2 capped at 2 mg, over one to five occasions. Blood was sampled
at 10, 20, 30, 40, 60, 75 and 140 min and at 24 h when still in hospital;
425 concentrations and 276 VIPN assessments were analysed.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Centanni_2024_vincristine")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each
`ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Centanni_2024_vincristine.R`
and `Centanni_2024_vincristine_mipd.R`. The table below collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (estimation model) | log(45.2) L/h at 70 kg | Table 2 CL |
| `lcl` (`_mipd`) | log(42.3) L/h at 70 kg | Results 'Pharmacokinetic Model' (90% group) |
| `e_cyp3a5_expr_cl` (`_mipd`) | 1.87, fixed | Methods 'Approximation of Non-estimated Factors' (79.1 / 42.3) |
| `lvc` | log(23.3) L | Table 2 Vc |
| `lq` | log(114) L/h | Table 2 Q |
| `lvp` | log(576) L | Table 2 Vp |
| `ltlag` | log(0.058) h | Table 2 LAGT (infusion only) |
| `tinf_mult` | 1.30 | Table 2 INFT |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed), 70 kg | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic Model'; Table 2 footnote a |
| `etalcl` (estimation model) | 0.4617 (76.6%) | Table 2 IIV CL |
| `etalcl` (`_mipd`) | 0.0992 (32.3%) | Results 'Pharmacokinetic Model' |
| `etalcl_oc1`-`etalcl_oc5` (`_mipd`) | 0.1238 (36.3%) | Results 'Pharmacokinetic Model' |
| `etalvc` | 0.4782 (78.3%) | Table 2 IIV Vc |
| `etaltlag` | 0.4016 (70.3%) | Table 2 IIV LAGT |
| `etaRUV` | 0.0765 (28.2%) | Table 2 IIV RUV (infusion samples) |
| `expSd_bolus` | 0.137 | Table 2 RUVadd,bolus (log scale) |
| `expSd_infusion` | 0.204 | Table 2 RUVadd,infusion (log scale) |
| `b1_vipn` | -121 | Table 3 B1\|0 |
| `b1_occ_vipn` | -119.54 | Table 3 B1\|0, if OCC > 1 (-120), refined from Figure S6 |
| `b2b1_nm_vipn` | -1.22 | Table 3 B2\|0 (neuropathy/motor) |
| `b2b1_cs_vipn` | -3.59 | Table 3 B2\|0 (constipation/sensory) |
| `b_prev_vipn` | 2.81 | Table 3 B > 0\|Grade > 0 |
| `emax_vipn` | 119 | Table 3 Emax |
| `auc50_vipn` | 0.164 ng\*h/mL | Table 3 prints 1.62; 0.164 from Figure S6 |
| Two-compartment ODEs, allometry | -- | Methods and Results 'Pharmacokinetic Model' |
| Proportional-odds logits | -- | Eqs. 2-5; Results 'Pharmacodynamic Model' |
| AUC = dose / CL | -- | Results 'Pharmacodynamic Model'; Methods Eq. 7 text |
| Omega from CV% | `log(1 + CV^2)` | Table 2 footnote b |

# Neuropathy model: Online Resource 2 (Figure S6)

Table 3 prints the two intercepts and Emax to three significant figures, but
the model uses them only as a near-cancelling sum (-121 + 119), so the
rounding moves the net logit by up to one unit. The paper's Online Resource 2
(Figure S6) plots P(grade >= 1) and P(grade >= 2) against AUC for six
scenarios, "calculated using the expit function and parameter estimates".
The maintainers traced the curves from the supplement's image (neuralgia/motor
increment) and fitted Eqs. 4-5 to them with Emax, AUC50 and the intercepts
free. The fit returned Emax = 119.0, B > 0|Grade > 0 = 2.81, B2|0 = -1.21 and
B1|0 + Emax = -2.01, all matching Table 3, plus an occasion > 1 intercept of
-119.54 (Table 3: -120) and an AUC50 of 0.164 ng\*h/mL, where Table 3 prints
1.62. The packaged model carries the refined intercept and AUC50 = 0.164.

The chunk below solves the packaged model on a grid of AUC values and
compares it with the traced points, and repeats the solve with the two
printed values (`b1_occ_vipn = -120`, `auc50_vipn = 1.62`).

```{r fig-s6-traced}
# Traced from Online Resource 2 (Figure S6), probabilities. Scenario codes:
# DRUG = first occasion, previous grade 0; OCC1 = occasion > 1; PDV =
# previous grade > 0. Grade 2 panel uses the neuralgia/motor increment.
traced <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~auc, ~p_ge1, ~p_ge2,
  "DRUG",       10, 0.0185, 0.0058,
  "DRUG",       20, 0.0491, 0.0153,
  "DRUG",       40, 0.0750, 0.0240,
  "DRUG",       75, 0.0935, 0.0298,
  "DRUG",      200, 0.1083, 0.0349,
  "DRUG_OCC1",  10, 0.0787, 0.0247,
  "DRUG_OCC1",  20, 0.1824, 0.0618,
  "DRUG_OCC1",  40, 0.2639, 0.0960,
  "DRUG_OCC1",  75, 0.3102, 0.1171,
  "DRUG_OCC1", 200, 0.3454, 0.1345,
  "PDV",        10, 0.2500, 0.0902,
  "PDV",        20, 0.4630, 0.2029,
  "PDV",        40, 0.5806, 0.2909,
  "PDV",        75, 0.6343, 0.3396,
  "PDV",       200, 0.6694, 0.3760,
  "PDV_OCC1",   10, 0.5852, 0.2960,
  "PDV_OCC1",   20, 0.7870, 0.5229,
  "PDV_OCC1",   40, 0.8556, 0.6385,
  "PDV_OCC1",   75, 0.8806, 0.6880,
  "PDV_OCC1",  200, 0.8972, 0.7222
)

mod <- readModelDb("Centanni_2024_vincristine")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(rxode2::rxode(mod))

scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,   ~CYCLE, ~PREV_AE_SCORE,
  "DRUG",           1, 0,
  "DRUG_OCC1",      2, 0,
  "PDV",            1, 1,
  "PDV_OCC1",       2, 1
)
# A 70 kg typical subject: AUC = dose / CL, so dose (mg) = AUC x 45.2 / 1000
auc_grid <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 5, seq(10, 250, by = 10))
s6_events <- tidyr::expand_grid(scen, auc = auc_grid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())
s6_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  s6_events |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = auc * 45.2 / 1000),
  s6_events |> dplyr::mutate(time = 24, evid = 0L, amt = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", WT = 70, TINF = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

solve_s6 <- function(params = NULL) {
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = s6_events, params = params,
                         keep = c("scenario", "auc"), returnType = "data.frame")
  dplyr::select(out, scenario, auc, auc_occ, p_vipn_ge1, p_vipn_ge2_nm)
}
s6_model <- solve_s6()
s6_printed <- solve_s6(c(b1_occ_vipn = -120, auc50_vipn = 1.62))

# The model's AUC is dose / CL of the subject, as in the paper
stopifnot(max(abs(s6_model$auc_occ / s6_model$auc - 1)) < 1e-6)

cmp_s6 <- traced |>
  dplyr::inner_join(s6_model, by = c("scenario", "auc")) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    s6_printed |> dplyr::select(scenario, auc,
                                printed_ge1 = p_vipn_ge1,
                                printed_ge2 = p_vipn_ge2_nm),
    by = c("scenario", "auc")
  )
err_model <- max(abs(c(cmp_s6$p_vipn_ge1 - cmp_s6$p_ge1,
                       cmp_s6$p_vipn_ge2_nm - cmp_s6$p_ge2)))
err_printed <- max(abs(c(cmp_s6$printed_ge1 - cmp_s6$p_ge1,
                         cmp_s6$printed_ge2 - cmp_s6$p_ge2)))
c(packaged_model = err_model, printed_table3 = err_printed)
# Deterministic: same equations, no random draws. The packaged values
# reproduce the authors' curves to tracing precision; the printed values
# miss them by tens of percentage points.
stopifnot(err_model < 0.02, err_printed > 0.3)
```

```{r fig-s6-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Online Resource 2 (Figure S6) of Centanni 2024
s6_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  s6_model |> dplyr::mutate(source = "Packaged model"),
  s6_printed |> dplyr::mutate(source = "Table 3 as printed")
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(p_vipn_ge1, p_vipn_ge2_nm), names_to = "grade",
                      values_to = "p") |>
  dplyr::mutate(grade = ifelse(grade == "p_vipn_ge1", "Grade >= 1",
                               "Grade >= 2 (neuralgia/motor)"))
traced_long <- traced |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(p_ge1, p_ge2), names_to = "grade", values_to = "p") |>
  dplyr::mutate(grade = ifelse(grade == "p_ge1", "Grade >= 1",
                               "Grade >= 2 (neuralgia/motor)"))
ggplot(s6_long, aes(auc, p, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = source)) +
  geom_point(data = traced_long) +
  facet_wrap(~grade, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "AUC (ng*h/mL)", y = "Probability", colour = "Scenario",
       linetype = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Points: traced from Online Resource 2 (Figure S6).\n",
                        "Lines: packaged model and Table 3 as printed.")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

The printed AUC50 of 1.62 ng\*h/mL is a factor of ten above the curves'
value; with it the model predicts almost no grade >= 2 VIPN at the protocol
doses (see the Table 4 section below), against the 5.8% at the first
occasion that the paper reports. The packaged value is 0.164.

# Virtual cohorts

The observed data are not public. Two cohorts are used, both built in base R
so that they are the same on every machine.

* **PK cohort** (Table 1 population): weight log-normal around the Table 1
  median of 34 kg (SD of log 0.45), truncated to the observed 12-95 kg; BSA
  from the weight-only Costeff formula `BSA = (4 WT + 7) / (WT + 90)`; one
  1.5 mg/m^2 dose capped at 2 mg; 100 subjects as an IV bolus and 100 as the
  protocol 60-min infusion, entered as its 38 min of vincristine
  (`TINF = 38/60`; see the next section).
* **ALL cohort** for the precision-dosing simulation (Methods 'Generation of
  the Target Populations'): ages 1-18 years weighted towards the 2-5-year
  incidence peak of childhood ALL, weight from a log-linear interpolation of
  median weight against age (8.9 kg at 1 year, 11.5 kg at 2 years, 27.1 kg at
  8.3 years and 70 kg at 18 years, the anchors of the Nijstad 2022
  vincristine article) with 15% scatter, Costeff BSA, 1.5 mg/m^2 capped at
  2 mg, high-clearance mixture group with probability 0.10; 200 subjects.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20240201)
n_arm <- 100
pk_subjects <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(2 * n_arm),
  arm = rep(c("Bolus", "60-min infusion"), each = n_arm),
  TINF = rep(c(0, 38 / 60), each = n_arm),
  WT = pmin(pmax(34 * exp(rnorm(2 * n_arm, 0, 0.45)), 12), 95)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    BSA = (4 * WT + 7) / (WT + 90),
    dose = pmin(1.5 * BSA, 2)
  )

obs_times <- c(0, 1 / 6, 1 / 3, 0.5, 2 / 3, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.33, 3, 4, 6,
               8, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72)
pk_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pk_subjects |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose,
                  rate = ifelse(TINF > 0, -2, 0)),
  tidyr::expand_grid(pk_subjects, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", CYCLE = 1, PREV_AE_SCORE = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
```

# PK simulation (Figure 1)

```{r simulate-pk}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240201)
sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = pk_events,
                          keep = c("arm", "dose", "BSA"),
                          returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates the layout of Figure 1 of Centanni 2024 (bolus and 60-min
# infusion over the sampling window); simulated percentiles only.
sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% setdiff(obs_times[obs_times <= 24], 0)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = quantile(sim, 0.10), p50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    p90 = quantile(sim, 0.90), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after start of administration (h)",
       y = "Vincristine (ng/mL)",
       caption = paste("Median and 10th-90th percentiles of simulated",
                       "observations; compare Figure 1 of Centanni 2024."))
```

## Infusion timing

`TINF` is the documented infusion duration, which the model stretches by
the estimated factor 1.30. The protocol infusion lasted 60 min, of which
38 min were vincristine and 22 min flushing, so the documented time could be
either. The typical-value solve below (34 kg, 1.8 mg) compares the two
readings with the observed median of Figure 1 (60-minute IV panel, read by
the maintainers): about 24 ng/mL from 0.25 to 0.8 h, about 9 ng/mL at 1.1 h
and about 3 ng/mL at 2.2 h.

```{r infusion-timing}
tt <- c(0.25, 0.55, 0.85, 1.13, 2.2)
timing_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(id = 1:2, TINF = c(38 / 60, 1), time = 0, evid = 1L,
                 amt = 1.8, rate = -2),
  tidyr::expand_grid(tibble::tibble(id = 1:2, TINF = c(38 / 60, 1)),
                     time = tt) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", WT = 34, CYCLE = 1, PREV_AE_SCORE = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
timing <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = timing_events,
                          returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = id, values_from = Cc) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fig1 = c(24, 24, 19, 9, 3))
timing |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time, "TINF = 38 min" = `1`,
                "TINF = 60 min" = `2`, "Figure 1 median (approx.)" = fig1) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(2, 1, 1, 0), caption = paste(
    "Typical concentrations (ng/mL) after a 1.8 mg infusion under the two",
    "readings of the documented infusion time."
  ))
```

With the 38-min drug time the infusion ends at about 0.9 h (38 min x 1.30
plus the 3.5-min lag) and the profile follows Figure 1; with 60 min it would
last 78 min, longer than the whole administration including the flush, and
the decline would come half an hour late. The vignette therefore enters the
standard infusion as `TINF = 38/60` h.

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA table. The check below runs PKNCA on the simulated
individual profiles (without residual error) and compares AUC0-inf with the
model's own `dose / CL`, and the body-surface-area-normalised clearance with
the approximately 23 L/h/m^2 that the Discussion derives from the estimated
CL.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, arm) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, arm, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, arm, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_df <- pk_events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose_ng = amt * 1e6) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, dose_ng, arm)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose_ng ~ time | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                          intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

auc_check <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    sim_pk |> dplyr::filter(time == 24) |>
      dplyr::select(id, auc_occ, cl, BSA),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (aucinf.obs / auc_occ - 1),
                cl_bsa = cl / BSA)
stopifnot(
  # A fast-clearing subject can fall below solver precision before 72 h and
  # lose its terminal phase; nearly all subjects must still give AUC0-inf
  mean(is.na(auc_check$pct_diff)) < 0.05,
  # AUC0-inf from the simulated profile against dose / CL of the same
  # subject: numerical (trapezoid and extrapolation) error only
  abs(median(auc_check$pct_diff, na.rm = TRUE)) < 5,
  quantile(abs(auc_check$pct_diff), 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) < 15
)

nca_wide |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cmax = median(cmax), tmax = median(tmax),
    aucinf = median(aucinf.obs, na.rm = TRUE),
    thalf = median(half.life, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)" = aucinf, "t1/2 (h)" = thalf
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2,
               caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters by arm (PKNCA).")
```

```{r cl-bsa}
tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = "CL / BSA (L/h/m^2)",
  Simulated = median(auc_check$cl_bsa),
  Published = 23
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = paste(
    "Median simulated BSA-normalised clearance against the Discussion's",
    "approximation of the estimated CL (Centanni 2024)."
  ))
```

The typical CL scaled to the cohort's median weight and BSA gives
45.2 x (34/70)^0.75 / 1.2 = 21.8 L/h/m^2, close to the paper's 23 L/h/m^2;
the simulated median also reflects the weight and BSA spread of the
virtual cohort.

# Precision-dosing simulation, standard dosing arm (Table 4)

The paper simulated 1000 children with ALL receiving 1.5 mg/m^2 (cap 2 mg)
over five occasions, with true exposures from the `_mipd` model (mixture,
IIV and IOV on CL), and reduced the next dose by 20% after any grade >= 2
VIPN. The standard-dosing ("No MIPD") column of Table 4 gives the incidence
of grade >= 2 VIPN (any subscore) per occasion. The model-informed arm needs
a Bayesian dose-adaptation loop and is not reproduced here.

Each occasion below is one deterministic solve of the `_mipd` model (random
effects drawn in base R and passed as parameters, so the cohort is
machine-independent) that returns the VIPN probabilities for a previous
grade of 0 and above 0; the four subscore chains are then sampled in R.

```{r table-4}
set.seed(20240202)
mod_mipd <- readModelDb("Centanni_2024_vincristine_mipd")
mod_mipd_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(rxode2::rxode(mod_mipd))
n_all <- 200
age_w <- c(3, 6, 6, 5, 4, 3.5, 3, 2.5, 2.2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2)
wt_anchor <- tibble::tibble(age = c(1, 2, 8.3, 18), wt = c(8.9, 11.5, 27.1, 70))
all_subjects <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_all),
  AGE = sample(1:17, n_all, replace = TRUE, prob = age_w) + runif(n_all),
  CYP3A5_EXPR = as.integer(runif(n_all) < 0.10),
  etalcl = rnorm(n_all, 0, sqrt(0.0992))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    WT = exp(approx(log(wt_anchor$age), log(wt_anchor$wt), log(AGE),
                    rule = 2)$y) * exp(rnorm(n_all, 0, 0.15)),
    BSA = (4 * WT + 7) / (WT + 90),
    dose = pmin(1.5 * BSA, 2)
  )
iov <- matrix(rnorm(n_all * 5, 0, sqrt(0.1238)), n_all, 5)

subscores <- c("neuralgia", "motor", "constipation", "sensory")
grade_prev <- matrix(0, n_all, 4, dimnames = list(NULL, subscores))
dose_now <- all_subjects$dose
tox_prev <- rep(FALSE, n_all)
inc <- numeric(5)
exp_occ1 <- NA_real_
for (occ in 1:5) {
  dose_now <- ifelse(tox_prev, dose_now * 0.8, dose_now)
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    all_subjects |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_now,
                                  PREV_AE_SCORE = 0),
    all_subjects |> dplyr::mutate(time = 1, evid = 0L, amt = 0,
                                  PREV_AE_SCORE = 0),
    all_subjects |> dplyr::mutate(time = 2, evid = 0L, amt = 0,
                                  PREV_AE_SCORE = 1)
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", TINF = 0, CYCLE = occ, OCC = occ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time)
  prm <- all_subjects |>
    dplyr::select(id, etalcl) |>
    dplyr::mutate(etalcl_oc1 = iov[, 1], etalcl_oc2 = iov[, 2],
                  etalcl_oc3 = iov[, 3], etalcl_oc4 = iov[, 4],
                  etalcl_oc5 = iov[, 5])
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mipd_typ, events = ev, params = prm,
                         returnType = "data.frame")
  p0 <- out[out$time == 1, ]
  p1 <- out[out$time == 2, ]
  tox <- rep(FALSE, n_all)
  p_none_ge2 <- rep(1, n_all)
  for (k in seq_along(subscores)) {
    prev_pos <- grade_prev[, k] > 0
    p_ge1 <- ifelse(prev_pos, p1$p_vipn_ge1, p0$p_vipn_ge1)
    p_ge2 <- if (subscores[k] %in% c("neuralgia", "motor")) {
      ifelse(prev_pos, p1$p_vipn_ge2_nm, p0$p_vipn_ge2_nm)
    } else {
      ifelse(prev_pos, p1$p_vipn_ge2_cs, p0$p_vipn_ge2_cs)
    }
    u <- runif(n_all)
    grade_prev[, k] <- ifelse(u < p_ge2, 2, ifelse(u < p_ge1, 1, 0))
    tox <- tox | grade_prev[, k] == 2
    p_none_ge2 <- p_none_ge2 * (1 - p_ge2)
  }
  # Occasion 1: every chain starts at grade 0, so the expected incidence is
  # exact given the cohort
  if (occ == 1) exp_occ1 <- 100 * mean(1 - p_none_ge2)
  inc[occ] <- 100 * mean(tox)
  tox_prev <- tox
}

table4 <- tibble::tibble(
  occasion = 1:5,
  simulated = inc,
  published = c(5.8, 31.3, 51.4, 60.6, 62.1)
)
table4 |>
  dplyr::rename("Occasion" = occasion,
                "Simulated grade >= 2 (%)" = simulated,
                "Table 4, no MIPD (%)" = published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = paste(
    "Incidence of grade >= 2 VIPN per occasion under standard dosing",
    "(1.5 mg/m^2, cap 2 mg, 20% reduction after grade >= 2)."
  ))
exp_occ1
stopifnot(
  # Occasion 1 expectation: with the printed AUC50 of 1.62 it is below 1%
  abs(exp_occ1 - 5.8) < 3,
  # Later occasions: centre of the four differences, robust to sampling
  abs(median(table4$simulated[2:5] - table4$published[2:5])) < 12
)
```

The first-occasion incidence is reproduced. Later occasions run a few
percentage points above Table 4; part of that is sampling noise at 200
subjects, part is the virtual ALL cohort, whose age and weight distribution
only approximates the paper's CDC-based sampling, and part is the sensitivity
to the occasion > 1 intercept described next.

# Target exposure (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows the probability of grade 0, 1 and >= 2 VIPN (any subscore),
averaged over five occasions, against a fixed AUC per occasion. With no
random effects in the VIPN model the subscore chains are independent Markov
chains, so the probabilities follow exactly from the model outputs by
propagating each chain's grade distribution.

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
f3_grid <- c(0, 2.5, 5, seq(10, 120, by = 10))
f3_events <- tidyr::expand_grid(scen, auc = f3_grid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())
f3_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  f3_events |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = auc * 45.2 / 1000),
  f3_events |> dplyr::mutate(time = 24, evid = 0L, amt = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", WT = 70, TINF = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

propagate <- function(params = NULL) {
  pr <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = f3_events, params = params,
                        keep = c("auc"), returnType = "data.frame")
  pr$first <- pr$CYCLE == 1
  pr$prev <- pr$PREV_AE_SCORE > 0
  res <- lapply(f3_grid, function(a) {
    pa <- pr[pr$auc == a, ]
    # state distribution (grade 0, 1, >= 2) per subscore group
    dist <- list(nm = c(1, 0, 0), cs = c(1, 0, 0))
    ge1 <- ge2 <- numeric(5)
    for (occ in 1:5) {
      p_none_ge2 <- 1
      p_none_ge1 <- 1
      for (grp in c("nm", "cs")) {
        row0 <- pa[pa$first == (occ == 1) & !pa$prev, ]
        row1 <- pa[pa$first == (occ == 1) & pa$prev, ]
        col2 <- if (grp == "nm") "p_vipn_ge2_nm" else "p_vipn_ge2_cs"
        trans <- function(r) c(1 - r$p_vipn_ge1, r$p_vipn_ge1 - r[[col2]], r[[col2]])
        d <- dist[[grp]]
        new <- d[1] * trans(row0) + (d[2] + d[3]) * trans(row1)
        dist[[grp]] <- new
        # two subscores per group, independent chains
        p_none_ge2 <- p_none_ge2 * (1 - new[3])^2
        p_none_ge1 <- p_none_ge1 * new[1]^2
      }
      ge2[occ] <- 1 - p_none_ge2
      ge1[occ] <- 1 - p_none_ge1
    }
    tibble::tibble(auc = a, ge1 = mean(ge1), ge2 = mean(ge2))
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(res)
}
f3 <- propagate()
f3_print <- propagate(c(b1_occ_vipn = -120, auc50_vipn = 0.164))

dplyr::bind_rows(
  f3 |> dplyr::mutate(model = "Packaged (B1|0, OCC > 1 = -119.54)"),
  f3_print |> dplyr::mutate(model = "B1|0, OCC > 1 = -120 (printed)")
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(ge1, ge2), names_to = "grade", values_to = "p") |>
  dplyr::mutate(grade = ifelse(grade == "ge1", "Grade >= 1", "Grade >= 2")) |>
  ggplot(aes(auc, p, colour = grade, linetype = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "AUC per occasion (ng*h/mL)",
       y = "P(VIPN), mean of 5 occasions",
       colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Replicates Figure 3 of Centanni 2024 as cumulative\n",
                        "probabilities of grade >= 1 and grade >= 2.")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")

f3 |> dplyr::filter(auc %in% c(10, 20, 50, 100, 120)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    f3_print |> dplyr::select(auc, ge2_printed = ge2), by = "auc"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("AUC (ng*h/mL)" = auc, "Grade >= 1" = ge1,
                "Grade >= 2" = ge2, "Grade >= 2, intercept -120" = ge2_printed) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = paste(
    "Mean probability over five occasions. Figure 3 reads about 0.18, 0.37",
    "and 0.45 for grade >= 2 at 20, 50 and 100 ng*h/mL."
  ))
```

Figure 3 lies between the two curves: about 0.18, 0.37 and 0.45 for grade
>= 2 at 20, 50 and 100 ng\*h/mL, against 0.28, 0.46 and 0.52 for the packaged
model and 0.17, 0.33 and 0.39 with the occasion > 1 intercept at its printed
-120. Figure S6 pins that intercept at -119.54 (its OCC1 curves sit 1.46
logit units above the first-occasion curves at every AUC), so the packaged
model keeps the Figure S6 value. Figure 3 was simulated from 1000 virtual
patients, and averaging over their exposure spread flattens the curve; the
paper's 50 ng\*h/mL target corresponds to about 0.46 in the packaged model.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **AUC50.** Table 3 prints 1.62 ng\*h/mL. The packaged 0.164 ng\*h/mL was
  fitted by the maintainers to the curves of Online Resource 2 (Figure S6),
  which the authors computed from the parameter estimates; the same fit
  recovers Emax, the Markov term, the grade >= 2 increment and the net
  first-occasion intercept of Table 3. With 1.62 the model predicts 0.6%
  grade >= 2 VIPN at the first occasion against the 5.8% of Table 4. No
  correction notice was found for the article (Europe PMC, 2026-10-29).
* **Occasion > 1 intercept.** Table 3 prints -120. The packaged -119.54 is
  the Figure S6 fit and rounds to the printed value; `b1_vipn = -121` and
  `emax_vipn = 119` are as printed. Because the intercepts and Emax nearly
  cancel, use the packaged values together.
* **Subscore groups.** Table 3 groups 'neuropathy/motor' against
  'constipation/sensory'. With sensory neuropathy in the second group, the
  first is read as neuralgia plus motor neuropathy, which is also how the
  2026 follow-up code groups them.
* **Residual error.** Table 2 reports the residual magnitudes as
  'RUVadd' on log-transformed data with IIV on the infusion residual. IIV on
  a residual magnitude is coded in NONMEM as a theta times `exp(eta)` with
  the epsilon variance fixed to 1, so 0.137 and 0.204 are read as standard
  deviations on the log scale (`lnorm`).
* **Infusion duration.** `TINF` is the documented infusion duration and the
  model infuses over `1.30 x TINF` after the lag time. The paper does not
  say whether the documented time of the 60-min infusion is the 38 min of
  vincristine or the full 60 min with the flush; the maintainers read it as
  the 38-min drug time, which matches the timing of Figure 1 (see 'Infusion
  timing'). Infusion dose records must carry `rate = -2`.
* **Mixture on CL.** The `_mipd` model carries the paper's latent two-group
  mixture as the `CYP3A5_EXPR` covariate (1 = high-clearance group); the
  paper fixed the group probability to 10% rather than genotyping, so
  population simulations should draw it as Bernoulli(0.10).
* **Occasion-level PK in the estimation model.** In `Centanni_2024_vincristine`
  the IIV on CL is drawn once per subject. Since the paper treated each
  dosing occasion as its own individual, give each occasion its own `id`
  to reproduce that structure, or use the `_mipd` model, which has explicit
  IOV.
* **Virtual cohorts.** The weight distributions, the Costeff BSA (the paper
  used DuBois with sampled heights), the ALL age weights and the
  weight-for-age anchors are assumptions of this article. The paper sampled
  ages from published ALL incidence and weight and height from CDC LMS
  tables with a weight-height correlation of 0.7.
* **Not reproduced.** The model-informed dosing arm of Table 4 and Figures
  4-5 (Bayesian estimation from three samples per occasion at 0.33, 6.5 and
  7.5 h, a 50 ng\*h/mL target with a 20% acceptance band) and the AUC
  accuracy comparison of MIPD against NCA.
* **Population table.** The text gives 20 bolus and 15 infusion patients;
  Table 1 labels the 20 (57%) row 'Patients with infusion'.
